evidence.paraphrase: The city is enclosed in a dome whose falling glass fragments are continuously patched by robotic dome weevils.
evidence.quote:
It was precipitation peculiar to a dome: feather-light
fragments showering harmlessly on the city from time to time. Dome
weevils, their metal arms reaching out with molten glass, roamed the
huge casserole, ceaselessly patching and repairing.

evidence.paraphrase: Establishes that people live inside a domed city where natural weather is not a normal concern.
evidence.quote:
But he was thinking about weather, which was an unusual subject to
begin with for a person living in a domed city.

evidence.paraphrase: Explains that the house shakes because Fownes illegally tapped into the dome's air-blower system, causing air buffeting.
evidence.quote:
He
had a bootleg pipe connected into the dome blower system, and the
high-pressure air caused some buffeting against the thin walls of the
house.

evidence.paraphrase: Describes the mechanical clockwork device Fownes built to simulate weather and time.
evidence.quote:
The downstairs closet was like a great watch case, a profusion of
wheels surrounding the Master Mechanism, which was a miniature see-saw
that went back and forth 365-1/4 times an hour.

evidence.paraphrase: Fownes activates his device and the view of the domed city is replaced by a simulated environment.
His machine creates an artificial sunset, moon, and garden illusion, betraying its electrical/mechanical nature.
evidence.quote:
Instead of an orange sun at perpetual high noon, there was a red sun
setting brilliantly, marred only by an occasional arcover which left
the smell of ozone in the air. There was also a gigantic moon.

evidence.paraphrase: Fownes has never experienced real roses or a real moon, contrasting dome life with unknown natural reality.
evidence.quote:
They were all purely speculative of course. He had no idea how a rose
really smelled--or looked for that matter. Not to mention a moon.

evidence.paraphrase: In this society conformity is enforced as a physical necessity and police hunt down eccentricity.
evidence.quote:
Lanfierre's job was to ferret out aberration. It couldn't be tolerated
within the confines of a dome. Conformity had become more than a social
force; it was a physical necessity.

evidence.paraphrase: Explains that humanity moved into domes because governments could not create a sound foreign policy, leading to self-containment.
evidence.quote:
Thus the
movement into domes began--_by common consent of the governments_. This
is known as self-containment.

evidence.paraphrase: Fownes proposes leaving the dome for the open outside world of prairies and space.
evidence.quote:
Fresh air, Mrs. Deshazaway?
Space? Miles and miles of space where the real-estate monopoly has
no control whatever? Where the _wind_ blows across _prairies_

evidence.paraphrase: Reference to an Open Country beyond the dome where geiger counters no longer register radiation.
evidence.quote:
they say
that somewhere out in the space and the roses and the moonlight,
the sleeping equinox yawns and rises because on a certain day it's
_vernal_ and that's when it roams the Open Country where geigers no
longer scintillate.

evidence.paraphrase: The dome's entire air supply is now being forced through Fownes's bedroom after the valve is turned.
evidence.quote:
the entire dome air supply
is now coming through my bedroom.

evidence.paraphrase: An artificial tornado forms and moves toward the wall of the dome.
evidence.quote:
The twister roared and moved out of the bedroom, out over the rear of
the house toward the side of the dome.

evidence.paraphrase: The dome's climate control fails as the twister grows, the artificial sun disappears and temperature collapses.
evidence.quote:
The artificial sun vanished behind the mushrooming twister.
Optimum temperature collapsed.

evidence.paraphrase: MacBride reacts with panic to the loss of the dome's controlled optimum conditions.
evidence.quote:
"These are _not_ Optimum Dome
Conditions!" the voice wailed. "The temperature is _not_ 59 degrees.
The humidity is _not_ 47%!"

evidence.paraphrase: Fownes compares the spinning cloud to a book illustration to identify the phenomenon.
evidence.quote:
Humphrey Fownes took out the dust jacket he'd found in the library. He
held it up and carefully compared the spinning cloud in his bedroom
with the illustration.

evidence.paraphrase: Describes the network of pipes and valve through which dome air creates winds in the house.
evidence.quote:
There were attic pipes connected
to wall pipes and wall pipes connected to cellar pipes, and they made
one gigantic skeleton that began to rattle its bones and dance as
high-pressure air from the dome blower rushed in, slowly opening the
Studebaker valve wider and wider....

evidence.paraphrase: The policeman Lanfierre has come to admire the rare eccentricity his job suppresses.
evidence.quote:
Lanfierre had become an admirer of eccentricity. He came to see that
genuine quirks were rare and, as time went on, due partly to his own
small efforts, rarer.
